item.title: Re: Staff Post: Open
item.content:encoded:
Sorry, what? As my first comment on this page notes, the iconography is Creative Commons-BY 3.0., sourced from thenounproject.com. The authors are Maxim Kulikov, AlfredoCreates.com, and Cole Townsend.

The photographs are in the public domain. There is no requirement to source or attribute public domain media, and I haven't documented the truly massive amount of said images I've used in my works since 2011 because of that.

EDIT: Here are the links to the two of the three pictures in question in this tale, God help us.

https://www.flickr.com/photos/saltonline/24693342579/

https://www.flickr.com/photos/internetarchivebookimages/14752891571/

EDIT 2: The image of the Seminole people standing used for Theography comes from the state government of Florida at https://www.floridamemory.com/ but I can't find it again. You'll either have to take that or someone will have to find it

If the images are not wholly your own, please post the image's source as a link (or links) in reply to this post and edit it into your first post in this discussion thread.

item.content:encoded:
Whoa. Wait. Really?

Moving past my shock to comment on the actual piece:

This has one trick, plays with it in a bunch of fun and unnerving ways, and puts us on a lurch before it can wear out. The edits are simple and subtle enough to freak me out in that "first showed up to the Foundation, what is this, everything is so creepy" sort of way I washed up in back in 2009.

So, yeah, upvoted and glad to see you around again.

Oh, Thou who burns in Heart for those who burn
In Hell, whose fires thyself shall feed in turn;
How long be crying, ‘Mercy on them, God!’
Why, who art Thou to teach, and He to learn?
